quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake lights before you slow down to warn the other driver.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake lights before you slow down to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flashing your brake lights before you slow down warns a tailgater. The other driver may not see road hazards ahead that require you to slow down.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At speeds over 55 mph.
After riding for several hours.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: What is the best group formation when riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway?

options.text: Pairs.
Single-file.
Staggered.
Passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. However, switch to single-file when riding through curves, through turns, or when entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. How does this affect motorcycle riders?

options.text: It is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
It is usually safe for motorcyclists unless it is raining.
It should always be avoided because other parts of the lane are safer.
It helps motorcycle tires grip better.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually safe for motorcyclists unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough traction for safe riding. The strip is often less than two feet wide, so you can ride around it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How should a rider sit for the best control of a motorcycle?

options.text: With arms fully extended.
Using arms to hold the body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: What should you do if the throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle is stuck, twist it back and forth several times. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Ride alongside the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If chased by a dog, downshift and approach it slowly. Then speed up and leave it behind. If you see a larger animal, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your following distance.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Stay flexible about your lane position at night.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Close to the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from having to chase the group. It also lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What is the best way to ride when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery at the start of rain because oil from cars has not yet washed away. It is safest to ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle with maximum braking power?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time to stop in a straight line with maximum power. Do not lock either wheel. Always use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: In motorcycle and car crashes, how many are caused by drivers not giving riders the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers fail to give riders the right-of-way.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your safety distance from other vehicles.
Ride in a weaving pattern back and forth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a position that makes it easy for other drivers to see you. Keep a safe distance so you can avoid danger if needed. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Squeeze the front brake suddenly to keep the tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: What kind of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces.
Shoes with short heels.
Shoes with tall heels.
Sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes with short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear strong, sturdy shoes that cover your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: How should you position your body during a slow, tight turn?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. But in slow, tight turns, keep your body upright to balance the leaning motorcycle.

questions.question: Is there a lane position that you should always avoid?

options.text: Yes, the left portion of the lane.
Yes, the center portion of the lane.
Yes, the right portion of the lane.
No, no lane position should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, no lane position should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position and no position you must always avoid. Choose your lane position based on the current riding conditions.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle rider position themselves in a traffic lane?

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position and no position you must always avoid. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When shifting into neutral gear.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is following you too closely, flash your brake light before you slow down. The driver behind you may not see hazards ahead that you are avoiding.

questions.question: What should you do about the oily strip in the center of the lane?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride only on it because it has better grip.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other debris in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from vehicles builds up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough grip for a motorcycle. On wet roads, avoid it. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still be in the center lane area.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the back of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead the group.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion
The shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing on the left. This helps you see better and makes oncoming traffic see you more easily.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Try to get onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding to the side of the passing driver is dangerous. Riding too far away might make them return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required for an effective eye or face shield?

options.text: It must fasten securely.
It must be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow clear side views.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear side views, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed. It should NOT be too tight.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
